mientas como Canva o Genially, o realice un cartel informati-
vo de forma manual si prefiere una opción offline . El producto
debe sintetizar los principios de uso responsable y justo para
ser compartido con la comunidad educativa. Esta actividad de
producción fomenta la competencia en comunicación visual
y ciudadanía digital.

Esta unidad persigue que los docentes comprendan la gobernan-
za como un sistema dinámico de toma de decisiones que regu-
la el uso ético y responsable de la IA en educación. El enfoque
parte del concepto de gobernanza multinivel *, que reconoce que
las decisiones sobre IA se toman simultáneamente en esferas glo-
bales, como las prescritas por la UNESCO o la Unión Europea, y
ministerios de educación nacionales y locales, requiriendo coor-
dinación entre estos niveles. El propósito de esta unidad es capa-
citar al profesorado para comprender y evaluar las estructuras de
poder y los marcos normativos que regulan la inteligencia artifi-
cial, permitiéndoles transitar de una posición de consumidores
tecnológicos a la de actores clave en la gobernanza y la toma de
decisiones democráticas en sus centros educativos.

rios propios de evaluación. Se incorpora el diseño universal para
el aprendizaje (DUA) al ofrecer múltiples formatos de acceso a
la información, como textos, infografías o ejemplos concretos, y
alternativas para docentes con distintos niveles de conectividad.

La pertinencia de esta unidad radica en que los docentes no
son simplemente usuarios finales de herramientas de IA, sino
también actores clave en su gobernanza escolar. Comprender los
mecanismos de decisión les permite incidir en políticas institu-
cionales, proteger los derechos de sus estudiantes y tomar deci-
siones pedagógicas informadas. La transferencia a la práctica se
materializa en la capacidad del docente para elaborar acuerdos
de aula sobre el uso de IA, identificar cuándo una herramienta
requiere autorización institucional y participar activamente en
comités de innovación tecnológica de su centro educativo.

La gobernanza internacional de la IA en educación se centra
en la cooperación entre diferentes regiones y culturas para esta-
blecer estándares éticos y regulatorios comunes. La Unión Eu-
ropea, por ejemplo, desarrolló un marco de gobernanza basado
en reglas éticas, estandarización y regulación estricta para pro-
mover un estándar global y proteger a los consumidores y usua-
rios (Hernández Peña, 2021). Además, se destaca la necesidad
de cooperación entre Europa, América del Norte y Asia Oriental
para superar barreras culturales y prácticas (ÓhÉigeartaigh et al.,
2020).
Una gobernanza efectiva no es posible sin la participación ac-
tiva y democrática de todos los actores del ecosistema educativo.
El Estado cumple un rol rector: debe diseñar marcos legales, fi-
nanciar infraestructuras tecnológicas y establecer mecanismos de
supervisión. Sin embargo, no debe actuar de forma imperativa.
Por otro lado, la experiencia de Canadá ilustra cómo el gobierno
federal colabora con provincias y universidades para crear cen-
tros de investigación en IA educativa, promoviendo redes de co-
nocimiento (Gobierno de Canadá, 2023).

La armonización y cooperación regional en la gobernanza
de la IA en educación se enfoca en superar barreras culturales
y prácticas para establecer estándares comunes. La cooperación
entre regiones es crucial para promover la confianza. Iniciativas
como la Casa de la Inteligencia Artificial en la Riviera Francesa

title: 125 Módulo 6. Políticas públicas y gobernanza de la IA en los sistemas educativos

paragraphs.text:
ejemplifican la colaboración regional para la aculturación de la
IA en el ecosistema educativo e industrial (Romero et al., 2024).
A nivel nacional, la gobernanza se traduce en políticas públicas
específicas que regulan el uso de IA en las instituciones educati-
vas. Cabe destacar el caso de Finlandia, que desarrolló una estra-
tegia nacional que incluye programas de formación docente en
competencias digitales y ética tecnológica.

Además, la rendición de cuentas* en la gobernanza de la IA
en el sistema educativo es un tema multifacético. Se define en
términos de responsabilidad de respuesta y se estructura en torno
a tres condiciones: reconocimiento de autoridad, interrogación
y limitación del poder, para lo cual se propuso una arquitectura
que persiga su cumplimiento, supervisión y ejecución (Novelli
et al., 2024).

La IA en la educación supone también enfoques basados en la
ciencia de datos y el aprendizaje automático (Gulson et al., 2024)
e implica la colaboración entre diferentes disciplinas. En concre-
to, las escuelas son responsables de integrar la IA en sus sistemas
de enseñanza y administración asegurando que se utilice de ma-
nera ética y efectiva (Çela et al., 2025).

title: Enfoque didáctico

paragraphs.text:
Esta unidad busca capacitar a los docentes para comprender las po-
líticas públicas como marcos protectores que garantizan derechos
fundamentales en el ecosistema digital educativo. El enfoque se
sustenta en el concepto de justicia algorítmica *, que reconoce que los
sistemas de IA pueden reproducir y amplificar desigualdades his-
tóricas si no se diseñan e implementan con criterios de equidad.

El marco conceptual integra tres dimensiones regulatorias in-
terdependientes: 1) la protección de datos, es decir, garantizar
privacidad y consentimiento informado; 2) la equidad algorítmi-
ca, que se trata de detectar y mitigar sesgos discriminatorios; y 3)
la soberanía educativa*, que consiste en preservar la autonomía
pedagógica frente a intereses comerciales. Estas dimensiones se
abordan desde una perspectiva que reconoce las particularidades
de nuestros sistemas educativos, incluyendo brechas digitales y
diversidad cultural.

title: 128 Alfabetización mediática para la integración educativa de la IA

paragraphs.text:
Metodológicamente, se aplica el aprendizaje mediante el aná-
lisis de casos reales de incidencias regulatorias en la región. Los
docentes examinan situaciones concretas como filtraciones de
datos estudiantiles o sesgos en sistemas de evaluación automa-
tizada para desarrollar criterios propios de análisis crítico. Se
incorpora la evaluación formativa mediante rúbricas de autoe-
valuación que permiten a los docentes calibrar su comprensión
progresiva de los marcos regulatorios.

La pertinencia de la alfabetización en IA radica en que los
docentes deben ser capaces de navegar entre marcos normativos
complejos para proteger a sus estudiantes y ejercer su autonomía
profesional. La transferencia a la práctica se concreta en habilida-
des como leer críticamente términos de servicio de plataformas
educativas, identificar cláusulas problemáticas en contratos ins-
titucionales con empresas tecnológicas y participar en procesos
de diseño de políticas escolares sobre el uso de IA.

Uno de los principales desafíos que enfrenta la integración
de la IA en la educación es la protección de datos personales y la
privacidad del estudiantado. Estos datos pueden incluir informa-
ción sensible como el historial académico, patrones de compor-
tamiento, interacciones en línea e incluso registros biométricos
en entornos de aprendizaje adaptativo. La recolección masiva de
estos datos, sin consentimiento informado ni transparencia sufi-
ciente, vulnera el derecho fundamental a la privacidad.

Por ejemplo, cuando una institución educativa adopta una he-
rramienta de redacción asistida por IA que almacena los trabajos
de los estudiantes en servidores externos, existe el riesgo de que
dichos datos sean utilizados con fines comerciales con terceros
sin el conocimiento del usuario. Este escenario es preocupante
en contextos donde las normativas de protección de datos son
débiles, como ocurre en regiones de América Latina (UNESCO,
2023). Otro desafío crítico son los sesgos algorítmicos. Los mo-
delos de IA son entrenados con grandes conjuntos de datos que
reflejan tendencias históricas y sociales, muchas veces marcadas
por desigualdades de género, raza, clase o discapacidad. Como
resultado, estas herramientas pueden reproducir y amplificar es-
tereotipos.

Por lo referido, los estudiantes deben contar con derechos di-
gitales plenos que incluyan el derecho a la explicación, el dere-
cho a la rectificación de errores algorítmicos y el derecho a no

title: 129 Módulo 6. Políticas públicas y gobernanza de la IA en los sistemas educativos

paragraphs.text:
ser sometidos a perfiles automatizados sin su consentimiento.
Estos derechos deben ser incorporados en las políticas educa-
tivas como pilares fundamentales de la justicia digital. De lo
contrario, la explotación de datos sensibles y la falta de supervi-
sión comprometen la integridad académica y la autenticidad del
aprendizaje (Kayyali, 2025).

Por otro lado, las grandes corporaciones tecnológicas inten-
sifican su presencia en el sector educativo mediante alianzas es-
tratégicas con gobiernos, donaciones de hardware , plataformas
gratuitas y programas de formación docente, lo que resulta en
primera instancia en oportunidades que pueden ocultar intere-
ses comerciales que pongan en riesgo la autonomía del sistema
educativo. Un ejemplo es Google, que promueve su suite Google
Workspace for Education, con herramientas de IA como Gemini
Education. Aunque estas herramientas facilitan la colaboración
y la gestión del aula, también permiten a la empresa recolectar
datos sobre estudiantes y docentes, lo que genera preocupaciones
sobre la privatización de la educación y la mercantilización del
conocimiento (Williamson, 2024). Además, estas corporaciones
suelen imponer sus propios modelos pedagógicos a través del
diseño de sus plataformas.

Por ello, es esencial que las políticas públicas incorporen me-
canismos de control y vigilancia sobre las alianzas público-pri-
vadas. Los contratos con empresas tecnológicas deben incluir
cláusulas de protección de datos, prohibición de uso comercial
de la información y garantías de interoperabilidad para evitar la
creación de monopolios digitales en el aula.

title: 133 Módulo 6. Políticas públicas y gobernanza de la IA en los sistemas educativos

paragraphs.text:
otras características. Su objetivo es asegurar que la IA sea justa y equi-
tativa para todos, evitando discriminaciones inherentes a los datos o
al diseño de los algoritmos.
* Privacidad por diseño. Un principio regulatorio que exige incor-
porar salvaguardas de protección de datos desde las primeras eta-
pas de desarrollo de herramientas tecnológicas, y no como añadidos
posteriores. Esto significa que la privacidad no es una opción, sino
una característica fundamental e integrada en el diseño de cualquier
sistema o aplicación.
* Rendición de cuentas algorítmica. Se refiere a los mecanismos que
permiten exigir responsabilidad a los desarrolladores y usuarios de
sistemas de IA cuando estos generan daños o discriminación. Incluye
el derecho a la explicación (entender cómo funciona un algoritmo)
y el derecho a la reparación (obtener una solución si un algoritmo
causa un perjuicio).
* Soberanía educativa digital. La capacidad de los sistemas educati-
vos para tomar decisiones autónomas sobre tecnologías digitales sin
subordinarse a intereses comerciales de corporaciones tecnológicas,
preservando así su misión pedagógica. Implica que las instituciones
educativas tienen el control sobre las herramientas y plataformas que
utilizan, priorizando los objetivos pedagógicos sobre los intereses
económicos.

title: Fundamentación y justificación

paragraphs.text:
En la actualidad, la inteligencia artificial (IA) ya no es un te-
lón de fondo técnico, sino todo un sistema social y mediático
que interviene en cómo se crean, circulan y valoran la informa-
ción y las historias (Frau-Meigs, 2024). Lejos de actuar como una
herramienta neutra, los sistemas algorítmicos participan en la
construcción social de la realidad al ordenar contenidos, sugerir
temas, traducir voces y hasta generar imágenes y vídeos. Esto im-
plica un doble reto: por un lado, comprender el papel de la IA en
los medios y, por otro, acompañar al alumnado en el desarrollo
de una mirada crítica y creativa ante estos procesos (Spinde et
al., 2024).

Este «Módulo 7: Inteligencia artificial y alfabetización
mediática» propone un marco accesible para explorar cómo la IA
reconfigura los medios tradicionales, cómo habilita (y tensiona)
prácticas de creación ciudadana —los llamados emirecs* , sujetos
que son a la vez emisores y receptores— y cuáles son los riesgos
asociados a los contenidos ultrafalsos (deepfakes) , los sesgos y la
manipulación algorítmica. La meta es dotar al lector de concep-
tos claros y estrategias didácticas que puedan trasladarse al aula
mediante actividades sencillas, seguras y pertinentes.

En primer lugar, abordaremos la IA y los medios tradicionales,
atendiendo a la transformación de las redacciones y la generación
de contenido audiovisual sintético. Analizaremos oportunidades
(accesibilidad, traducción, apoyos en la edición) y límites (trans-
parencia, trazabilidad, impacto laboral), así como pautas de uso
responsable y señales de advertencia para enseñar al estudianta-

do a preguntarse siempre quién lo ha producido, cómo y con qué
herramientas. (Baker y Hawn, 2021).

En segundo lugar, trataremos la IA y los emirecs , y las herra-
mientas generativas que facilitan la creación de textos, imágenes,
audio y vídeo. Nos centraremos en la democratización creativa
y sus dilemas (autoría, plagio, consentimiento de imagen/voz,
licencias) y en cómo las lógicas de recomendación moldean la
visibilidad de lo que publicamos. Aquí el enfoque será práctico:
pequeñas producciones guiadas y comparaciones entre lo que el
algoritmo premia y lo que favorece el diálogo y la inclusión (Poe-
ll, Nieborg y Duffy, 2021).

Por último, trabajaremos en contenidos ultrafalsos (deepfakes) ,
sesgos y manipulación algorítmica con una aproximación forma-
tiva y preventiva: reconoceremos indicios básicos de falsificación,
comprenderemos de dónde vienen los sesgos (datos, diseño, uso)
y practicaremos hábitos de verificación, fact-checking y cuidado
en la difusión. Todo ello, a sabiendas de que los sistemas de IA
no son neutrales, sino que favorecen ciertos usos del lenguaje y
marginan otros, reproduciendo desigualdades lingüísticas y cul-
turales (Bender et al., 2021; Blodgett et al., 2020). El objetivo es
que el profesorado aprenda a detectar, contextualizar y actuar
ante contenidos problemáticos, fortaleciendo su criterio y su par-
ticipación responsable en la vida digital.

En conjunto, el módulo ofrece un itinerario crítico y creativo,
enfocado en el empoderamiento (Sánchez-López et al., 2021):
entender cómo la IA interviene en nuestra experiencia mediática
y en la generación de contenidos, y protegernos frente a prácticas
de manipulación. Todo ello con propuestas didácticas realistas,
listas para el aula y orientadas a reforzar la alfabetización mediá-
tica desde edades tempranas.

sual creado con IA generativa, evaluando su claridad, accesi-
bilidad y necesidad de transparencia.
 Aplicar criterios responsables para el uso de la síntesis de voz*
comparando resultados y estableciendo condiciones adecua-
das para su empleo en contextos educativos o divulgativos.

title: Enfoques didácticos

paragraphs.text:
Tras el entusiasmo inicial por la magia de la automatización, hoy
sabemos que la integración de la IA en los medios de comunica-
ción —desde la redacción hasta la verificación o la creación de
materiales audiovisuales— abre posibilidades interesantes (ma-
yor accesibilidad, rapidez en ciertas fases, apoyo en la claridad),
pero también plantea riesgos evidentes, como la opacidad, la de-
pendencia tecnológica o la reproducción de sesgos. Para que pue-
da entender y situarse de manera responsable en el uso de estas
herramientas, esta unidad adopta un enfoque didáctico triple:
experiencial-operativo, analítico-crítico y creativo-propositivo.

El enfoque experiencial-operativo propone que explore de
primera mano cómo funciona la producción asistida median-
te actividades individuales muy acotadas: la redacción de una
noticia breve con y sin apoyo de IA, la comprobación básica de
afirmaciones a través de fuentes fiables y la elaboración de un
minivídeo con aviso de contenido sintético*. Estas prácticas per-
miten conocer las herramientas en contextos reales, documentar
las decisiones tomadas y observar diferencias de tiempo, claridad
o transparencia entre los procesos manuales y los procesos asis-
tidos.

El enfoque analítico-crítico ayuda a comprender qué hay
detrás de los resultados generados por IA. Se invita a formular
preguntas sencillas pero esenciales: de dónde salen los datos,
qué tipo de decisiones delega la herramienta, cómo comunica
sus límites, cómo deben verificarse sus propuestas y qué posi-
bles sesgos o errores puede introducir en una pieza informativa

Por último, el enfoque creativo-propositivo anima al profeso-
rado a utilizar la IA como un recurso para mejorar la comunica-
ción educativa. En las actividades de ampliación, se experimenta
con la síntesis de voz para valorar cuándo resulta apropiada en
contextos de accesibilidad o divulgación, y se propone redactar

claros de transparencia, consentimiento y responsabilidad en el
uso de herramientas generativas. El objetivo es que la tecnolo-
gía no sustituya la mirada pedagógica, sino que la complemente,
permitiendo crear materiales más inclusivos, rigurosos y com-
prensibles para todo tipo de públicos.

Para consolidar el aprendizaje, resulta útil trabajar con anda-
miajes simples (plantillas de titular, checklists de verificación, eti-
quetas de transparencia) y con evaluación formativa: pequeñas
evidencias de proceso, como una bitácora de decisiones (fuentes
consultadas, cambios aplicados, dudas detectadas). En contex-
tos de baja conectividad, estas prácticas pueden realizarse sin IA:
con recortes impresos, guiones en papel y comparaciones entre
versiones. Así, la unidad se orienta a que el profesorado integre
hábitos de rigor, accesibilidad (subtítulos, lectura fácil) y respon-
sabilidad mediática.

title: Actividades

paragraphs.text:  Redacción rápida con y sin IA. Busque un pequeño conjunto

de materiales sobre un acontecimiento actual (una nota breve,
una cita y uno o dos datos básicos). Con esa información, ela-
bore primero una noticia muy corta —un titular y unas pocas
líneas— escrita únicamente a mano. A continuación, utilice
una herramienta de IA para generar una segunda versión del
mismo texto, ya sea sugiriendo titulares o proponiendo una
entradilla alternativa. Tras producir ambas versiones, se invita
a reflexionar sobre el proceso con una pequeña lista de com-
probación: qué decisiones ha tomado la persona, qué elemen-
tos ha generado la IA y qué diferencias se aprecian entre am-
bas noticias en términos de claridad, tiempo de elaboración y
precisión. La actividad se completa incorporando una etiqueta

title: 138 Alfabetización mediática para la integración educativa de la IA

paragraphs.text:
de transparencia en la pieza asistida («Este texto fue realizado
con apoyo de IA»).
 Verificación básica y trazabilidad de afirmaciones. Una vez

elaborada la noticia, seleccione tres afirmaciones concretas
que puedan comprobarse de manera sencilla: una fecha, una
cifra, un hecho o un dato contextual. Para cada una, consul-
te dos fuentes fiables (preferiblemente medios contrastados o
páginas oficiales) y valore su grado de fiabilidad mediante un
semáforo muy simple: verde si coincide con las fuentes, ámbar
si presenta dudas o matices, rojo si es incorrecta. El ejercicio
culmina con un breve informe donde se explica qué se ha ve-
rificado, qué correcciones han sido necesarias, dónde se ha
buscado la información y en qué fecha. De este modo, obtie-
ne una primera experiencia práctica de trazabilidad y puede
observar cómo se fortalece una pieza informativa mediante la
verificación.
 Creación de un minivídeo con aviso de contenido sintético.

Esta actividad consiste en producir un pequeño clip que resu-
ma la noticia anterior. Para ello puede emplear herramientas
de IA generativa de vídeo. Se establecen tres reglas básicas:
evitar el uso de rostros reales sin permiso, mantener apoyos
visuales que aseguren la comprensión e incluir un aviso claro
que informe de la presencia de contenido sintético. Una vez
generado el clip, revíselo de forma crítica: ¿el mensaje es com-
prensible? ¿Las imágenes seleccionadas son adecuadas para
el contenido? ¿El aviso de transparencia queda bien visible?
Es una forma rápida de familiarizarse con las posibilidades
audiovisuales de estas herramientas sin necesidad de conoci-
mientos técnicos.

resultar útil en contextos educativos, por ejemplo, para cues-
tiones de accesibilidad o traducción. Reflexione también sobre

title: Objetivos

paragraphs.text:  Identificar los principales sistemas de creación textual, visual,

sonora y audiovisual para evaluar su accesibilidad y sus usos
potenciales por parte de usuarios no especializados.
 Analizar los procesos de democratización en la creación mul-

timodal para valorar su impacto en la participación ciudadana
y en la producción cultural distribuida.
 Reflexionar críticamente sobre los fenómenos de viralidad* y

las dinámicas algorítmicas para reconocer cómo influyen en
la visibilidad, circulación y lectura pública de los contenidos.

title: Enfoques didácticos

paragraphs.text:
Este apartado se basa en una secuencia de tres momentos —ex-
plorar, analizar y reinterpretar— para que el profesor pueda ex-
perimentar de forma autónoma con herramientas generativas
accesibles y, al mismo tiempo, desarrollar una mirada crítica so-
bre cómo influyen en la producción y circulación del contenido
digital.

En primer lugar, el enfoque experiencial-operativo se orienta
a la generación de textos, imágenes, audios o vídeos sencillos
mediante herramientas no-code / low-code , registrando prompts ,
ajustes y decisiones. El objetivo es comprender los mecanismos
básicos de la creación multimodal y reconocer cómo la IA inter-
viene en cada paso.

A continuación, el enfoque analítico-crítico invita a exami-
nar de qué manera los algoritmos condicionan la visibilidad. Se
propone analizar señales como el tipo de título, el ritmo narra-
tivo, la interacción que promueven y los patrones que favorecen
la viralidad. Esta lectura crítica permite cuestionar qué tipo de
contenidos premian las plataformas y qué modelos comunicativos
se reproducen.

Por último, el enfoque creativo-propositivo anima a reinter-
pretar lógicas virales con un propósito educativo o cívico. Diseñe
piezas con utilidad social; cuide las licencias, la accesibilidad y
los avisos de contenido sintético, y elabore criterios propios para
publicar de forma segura y responsable. La meta es que la creati-
vidad mediada por IA no sea un fin estético, sino una herramien-
ta de servicio comunitario.

Desde la alfabetización mediática, el concepto de emirec ayu-
da a situar al profesorado como acompañante de un alumnado
que no solo consume, sino que produce y distribuye mensajes.
La IA amplifica esta capacidad al reducir barreras técnicas, pero
también introduce dilemas de autoría, licencias y consentimien-
to (imagen, voz y datos). Por ello, el enfoque propone explicitar
siempre la procedencia de materiales, distinguir entre inspiración
y copia y promover la atribución cuando se adapten recursos.

En términos pedagógicos, se recomienda una progresión de
complejidad: primero, comprender la herramienta y registrar de-
cisiones. Después, reflexionar sobre el efecto de títulos, formatos
y recomendaciones. Por último, producir piezas con propósito

title: Actividades

paragraphs.text:  GeneraLab 3×30: creación con IA y bitácora individual. Rea-

lice tres micropiezas sobre historias locales cercanas apoyán-
dose en herramientas de IA generativa: un texto breve (nota
o guion), una imagen (cartel o ilustración) y un pequeño clip
audiovisual. Registre los prompts utilizados, las variaciones ge-
neradas y las decisiones tomadas. Identifique con precisión
qué parte ha sido producida por IA e incluya un aviso visible
de contenido sintético. El objetivo es entender cómo se articu-
la una creación básica y reconocer la trazabilidad de cada paso.
 Twin-post A/B: viralidad y diálogo. Seleccione dos publicacio-
nes sobre un mismo tema:
– Una orientada a maximizar alcance e impacto.
– Otra orientada a promover diálogo y comprensión.

Compare métricas simples ( likes , comentarios, ritmo de inte-
racción) y realice una lectura crítica del comportamiento al-
gorítmico: ¿qué está premiando la plataforma? ¿Qué favorece
una participación significativa? Esta comparación permite
analizar cómo se construye la visibilidad digital.
 Tendencias con propósito: reinterpretación responsable.

Identifique un formato viral (transición visual, plantilla sono-
ra, reto breve) y genere una versión que transmita un mensaje
cívico o educativo: convivencia, sostenibilidad, salud, lectura,
participación... Aplique estas reglas: no reproducir estereoti-
pos, no mostrar personas identificables sin consentimiento,
añadir subtítulos y citar fuentes si adapta materiales preexis-
tentes. El objetivo es ejercitar una apropiación creativa que
añada valor social.

title: Objetivos

paragraphs.text:  Reconocer los riesgos y desafíos asociados a la creación y di-

fusión de contenido falso generado con IA, especialmente en
casos de deepfake , para actuar con prudencia informativa.

tivos y contextos vulnerables.
 Examinar la influencia de algoritmos de recomendación y

clasificación en la manipulación de la opinión pública para
detectar burbujas informativas* y dinámicas de polarización.

title: Enfoque didáctico

paragraphs.text:
Este apartado se articula en torno a tres dimensiones comple-
mentarias: una aproximación de detección forense-ciudadana,
un análisis crítico del sesgo y una orientación propositiva hacia
la creación de protecciones educativas.

En la fase de detección forense, se propone que el profesorado
explore métodos accesibles para revelar signos de manipulación
y falsedad: incoherencias visuales, artefactos de audio, desajustes
de sincronía o inconsistencias contextuales. El objetivo es apren-
der a sospechar con método , contrastar fuentes y ejercitar decisio-

title: 145 Módulo 7. Inteligencia artificial y alfabetización mediática

paragraphs.text:
nes informadas sobre qué no compartir cuando existan dudas
razonables.

Posteriormente, en la fase analítico-crítica, se amplía la mi-
rada hacia los lugares donde se puede producir el sesgo con la
IA: datos, modelo, interfaz, sistemas de recomendación y comu-
nidad. Se orienta al análisis de cómo las decisiones técnicas y la
composición de las plataformas afectan a distintos colectivos y
cómo ciertos patrones pueden amplificar discriminaciones pre-
existentes.

Por último, en la fase propositiva, se invita a diseñar proteccio-
nes y salvaguardas: protocolos personales de verificación, listas
de señales de alerta, pautas de accesibilidad y criterios explícitos
para un uso seguro y transparente de contenidos sintéticos. La
meta es pasar de la detección a la acción educativa responsable.

Este enfoque pone especial atención en la seguridad y el cui-
dado (uso de materiales curados, respeto a la privacidad, lengua-
je no estereotipado y accesibilidad en todo el proceso).

En una alfabetización docente orientada a la prevención, la
prioridad no es solo cazar falsedades complejas, sino desarrollar
hábitos sostenibles: detenerse, contextualizar, verificar y cuidar.
Esto implica comprender que los deepfakes son solo una parte del
problema: la desinformación también se apoya en recortes, títu-
los engañosos, sesgos de selección y sistemas de recomendación
que personalizan la exposición informativa.

Didácticamente, el enfoque se apoya en andamiajes muy con-
cretos (matrices de indicios, semáforo de autenticidad, árbol de
decisión comparto / no comparto ) y en metacognición: explicar por
qué algo parece fiable o dudoso. Para trabajar con seguridad, se
sugiere utilizar materiales curados por el docente, evitar conteni-
dos sensibles y proteger la privacidad (sin rostros reales ni datos
personales). En baja conectividad, puede trasladarse el mismo
aprendizaje mediante capturas impresas, análisis de casos y pro-
tocolos de aula. La transferencia se completa cuando el profeso-
rado define un procedimiento breve para su centro o materia:
qué pasos seguir ante un contenido sospechoso, qué evidencias
pedir y cómo integrar la verificación como práctica habitual, no
como actividad excepcional.

De este modo, la unidad refuerza la autonomía docente para
orientar conversaciones difíciles, sostener una cultura de veri-

title: Actividades

paragraphs.text:  Clínica de deepfakes : detección forense básica. Realice una

búsqueda de imágenes, audios y clips breves susceptibles de
estar manipulados o generados con IA. Aplique una matriz
de indicios simples (visual, sonoro, contextual) y clasifique
cada contenido con un semáforo de autenticidad (verde/ám-
bar/rojo). Elabore un pequeño árbol de decisión personal: qué
comprobar primero, cómo contrastar y en qué momento de-
cidir no compartir.
 Jardín de burbujas: simulación de personalización. Trabaje

con varios perfiles informativos con diferentes perspectivas,
cada uno con un muro de publicaciones diferenciado. Observe
qué temas aparecen o desaparecen, qué tono domina y cómo
cambia la percepción al alternar entre perfiles. A partir de la
comparación, elabore un mapa de ausencias y proponga estra-
tegias de diversificación: ampliar fuentes, modular tiempos de
lectura, introducir preguntas de verificación.
 Mapa del sesgo: localización y mitigación. Analice un caso

sencillo de sesgo (por ejemplo, una herramienta que ofrece
ejemplos poco diversos). Dibuje la cadena del sesgo identifi-
cando: a) dónde cree que surge; b) cómo cree que se amplifica;
y c) tres posibles mitigaciones.

paragraphs.text:
* Burbujas informativas. Fenómeno por el cual los algoritmos de per-
sonalización exponen a las personas únicamente a contenidos afines
a sus creencias previas, limitando el acceso a perspectivas diversas y
reforzando visiones parciales de la realidad.
* Contenido sintético. Material digital en formato texto, imagen, au-
dio o vídeo generado total o parcialmente mediante sistemas de inte-
ligencia artificial, sin corresponder a una captura directa del mundo
real.
* Deepfakes. Contenidos audiovisuales manipulados mediante inteli-
gencia artificial que alteran de forma ultrarrealista la apariencia, voz
o acciones de personas, dificultando la distinción entre lo auténtico
y lo falso.
* Emirecs. Término que designa a usuarios de medios digitales que
actúan simultáneamente como emisores y receptores de contenido,
combinando la creación, el consumo y la difusión de información.
* Síntesis de voz. Tecnología que permite generar voz artificial a partir
de texto escrito mediante inteligencia artificial, utilizada en aplicacio-
nes de accesibilidad, traducción y locución automática.

title: Alfabetización mediática para la integración educativa de la IA Propuesta formativa para docentes

paragraphs.text:
En un contexto mediático y educativo marcado por la so-
breabundancia de contenidos, la automatización de tareas y
la expansión acelerada de la inteligencia artificial, esta obra
ofrece una propuesta formativa rigurosa, crítica y aplicada
para el profesorado. Lejos de concebir la IA como una simple
herramienta, el libro la sitúa como un fenómeno cultural,
tecnológico y pedagógico que redefine la manera en que se
produce, distribuye y comprende el conocimiento.

A lo largo de siete módulos, el texto articula un itinerario
que combina fundamentos técnicos accesibles con una sólida
reflexión ética, mediática y didáctica. Desde la comprensión
de algoritmos, datos y modelos de aprendizaje automático,
hasta el análisis de sesgos, la gobernanza algorítmica o el im-
pacto de los deepfakes, la obra proporciona claves para inter-
pretar críticamente los sistemas inteligentes que ya operan en
las aulas.

El núcleo de la propuesta reside en la alfabetización me-
diática como eje integrador: una competencia imprescindible
para formar ciudadanos capaces de analizar, evaluar y crear
información en entornos mediados por IA. En este sentido,
el libro no solo interpela al docente como usuario de tecno-
logía, sino como profesional que toma decisiones fundamen-
tadas, preserva su juicio pedagógico y promueve prácticas
educativas más justas, inclusivas y reflexivas.

Con un enfoque eminentemente práctico, cada módulo
incorpora actividades, estrategias didácticas y orientaciones
de evaluación transferibles al aula. Esta obra se presenta así
como una guía imprescindible para quienes buscan integrar
la inteligencia artificial en educación sin renunciar a una mi-
rada crítica, ética y humanista.

title: Executive Summary

paragraphs.text:
This report provides an analysis and strategic roadmap for the
integration of Artificial Intelligence (AI) within Türkiye’s educational
sector. The study aims to map the existing AI and EdTech landscape, evaluate
the nation’s technological readiness, and provide actionable recommendations
to guide policymakers. By focusing on an equitable, scalable, and responsive
adoption of AI, the report showcases new technologies to enhance teacher
effectiveness and improve learning for students across the country.

The methodology followed a multi-faceted data collection
approach conducted between July and October 2025 , involving in-depth
interviews with senior education policymakers, alongside a rigorous analysis
of secondary data sources regarding digital infrastructure, educational
performance, and EdTech penetration. Furthermore, a literature review of
education policies was conducted to ensure that the recommendations align
with global best practices and Türkiye’s specific context.

The report identifies a dynamic landscape of public and private
innovation, structured by a clear national AI framework, yet constrained
by systemic gaps that challenge equitable scaling:

•
Türkiye’s integration of AI into its education system is characterized by
proactive and systemic leadership from the Ministry of National Education,
anchored by the National AI Strategy (2021–2025) and the AI in Education
Policy Document and Action Plan (2025–2029), which prioritize a
homegrown technological ecosystem.
•
The Ministry of National Education has integrated AI into the education
system through initiatives to enhance learning. Central to this effort is
the EBA Student Assistant, an AI-powered tutoring system that provides
students with personalized support.
•
An important innovation in Türkiye’s educational landscape is the
establishment of the Education Technology Incubation and Innovation
Center (ETKİM), a strategic hub for EdTech innovation and a pillar of the
nation’s digital transformation.
•
The private sector in Türkiye operates within a high growth yet constrained
EdTech market. While local firms have developed specialized tools like
Madlen to provide feedback and personalized learning for students, such
innovations remain confined to metropolitan areas where families can
afford subscription-based services. Without clear pathways for public-
private partnerships, the scale of the private sector is limited.

The success of Türkiye’s AI initiatives depends on the continued
synchronization of policy, infrastructure, and human capital development .
The evidence indicates that while the technical architecture for an AI-
enhanced system is largely in place, the “readiness gap” among the teaching
workforce remains the primary variable for long-term impact. By grounding
the technological rollout in rigorous data governance and targeted teacher
upskilling, Türkiye aims to build a resilient educational infrastructure capable
of meeting the demands of an increasingly digital global economy.

title: 1. Introduction

paragraphs.text:
The integration of AI into the education sector holds immense
potential to impact pedagogical approaches, learning outcomes, and
administrative processes . This report explores the significance of AI in
Türkiye’s K-12 education, studying the global and European landscape of
AI adoption in schools, and providing an overview of Türkiye’s educational
context, including its current challenges and opportunities for AI integration.

AI technologies are increasingly being adopted in K-12 education
to personalize learning experiences, provide intelligent tutoring systems,
automate administrative tasks, and offer data-driven insights into student
performance. This shift from “novel innovation” to integrated institutional
adoption has been reported in Europe; according to the self-reported data, in
2024, 30% of education institutions have deployed at least one AI solution, up
from 25% in the prior year, and an additional 35% had completed an AI pilot. 1

Concerns regarding data privacy, ethical implications, and the
potential impact on critical thinking skills persist . As AI progressively
automates routine tasks, there is a growing emphasis on developing skills
that are uniquely human, such as critical thinking, creativity, and emotional
intelligence. 2 That said, Europe has been a leader in advocating ethical
guidelines for AI in education. The EU published “Ethics Guidelines on AI and
Data in Teaching and Learning”, giving schools and universities a framework
to evaluate AI tools – an accomplishment in providing moral leadership. 3 The
prevailing sentiment of the integration of AI in education is one of cautious
adoption, recognizing AI’s capacity to tailor education to individual student
needs and enhance overall efficiency.

Opportunities for AI integration in education are guided by
government policy regulations and strategy , such as the National Artificial
Intelligence Strategy (2021-2025), and the recent Artificial Intelligence in
Education Policy Document and Action Plan (2025–2029) developed by
Türkiye’s Ministry of National Education. Following these national policy
documents is critical to ensure that AI tools are used in a way that is inclusive,
ethical and aligned with Türkiye’s educational priorities. The National AI
Strategy and the AI in Education Policy Document provide a framework that
promotes accessibility and data privacy, while also supporting schools and
teachers adopt AI technologies responsibly and effectively. By following
these strategic guidelines, schools can contribute to a sustainable digital
transformation of the education sector.

AI in K-12 education , drawing upon insights from the brief, “AI Revolution
in Education: What You Need to Know,” while expanding the scope to offer
a distinct and in-depth examination of the topic, covering a wide range of

title: 2.1 TÜRKIYE’S EDTECH CONTEXT

paragraphs.text:
Türkiye’s internet penetration reached over 86% in 2024, 5 but access
remains uneven between urban and rural schools . Rural regions, which
account for more than one-fifth of Türkiye’s population, often face unreliable
connectivity, limited broadband coverage, and fewer digital resources compared
to metropolitan areas. 6 A study conducted in 2023 showed the magnitude of
the urban–rural digital gap by analyzing how digital readiness varies between
urbanized regions and rural provinces. Using a composite Digital Divide Index
that incorporates broadband availability, internet speed, computer ownership,
and ICT use, the study reports that while Türkiye’s major metropolitan centers
exhibit high levels of connectivity and digital adoption, rural and less-developed
eastern provinces suffer from minimal ICT infrastructure and very low digital
adoption. 7 This rural–urban divide means that while students in urban areas
benefit from EdTech platforms and AI-supported applications, those in smaller
towns and villages may struggle with access to online learning.

The digital divide is tied to socioeconomic disparities and underlying
financial inequalities . Families in rural areas are less able to afford AI-enabled
devices or subscription-based learning platforms, creating barriers to equitable
participation in digital education. This gap reinforces existing inequalities, as
students in urban areas gain competitive advantages in digital skills and exposure
to emerging technologies, while students in rural schools risk being left behind.

Building on the outcomes of the 2024 forum, the Türkiye Education
Technology Summit (TETZ) 2025 in Istanbul hosted a Ministerial Session
with ten countries to address the integration of AI in education. The
session’s conclusions emphasized that AI’s role extends beyond content
delivery to the development of “AI literacy” and digital competences, ensuring
students are prepared for the needs of the 21st century. Key strategic priorities
identified include reducing digital inequalities, developing large language
models compatible with local languages, and implementing data security
and ethical principles. Emphasizing a human-centric approach, Minister
of National Education Mr. Yusuf Tekin underlined that the AI integration
in education must respect cultural identities and diversity to ensure that
technological advancement is supported by a value-based vision. 9 By taking
the initiative to organize high-level ministerial sessions, Türkiye strategically
positions itself as a regional leader in the advancement of artificial intelligence
and digital education.

Besides the forums and Ministerial Sessions, Türkiye’s Ministry of
National Education has also developed the country’s AI strategic plan:
Artificial Intelligence in Education Policy Document and Action Plan (2025–
2029) , outlining a comprehensive guide for incorporating AI technologies into
the national education system. Aligned with the Türkiye Century Education
Model and the National AI Strategy, the plan emphasizes a human-centered,
ethical, inclusive, and sustainable approach to digital transformation in
education. It sets forth four strategic goals, fifteen policies, and forty action
steps aimed at enhancing learning personalization, supporting teacher
development, improving assessment and guidance systems, and ensuring
data privacy and transparency. The document highlights ongoing initiatives—
such as elective AI courses, teacher toolkits, and specialized AI learning
labs—and promotes international alignment with OECD, UNESCO, and EU
AI standards. Considering these strategies and roadmaps, the MoNE has
taken active steps to align K–12 education with this vision by promoting AI
awareness and competence among students and teachers.

Türkiye’s approach to incorporating AI into education is guided by
the National Artificial Intelligence Strategy (2021–2025), 10 which identifies
as one of its six key pillars the “ training experts equipped with advanced AI skills
and harmonization of the education system” and emphasizes the development
of AI literacy across all levels of education. This AI Strategy is also aligned with
Türkiye’s Education Vision 2023, a roadmap developed by The Ministry of
National Education (MoNE) to advance the nation’s education that aimed to

title: 2.3 MULTI-STAKEHOLDER EFFORTS TO EMBED AI IN TÜRKIYE’S EDUCATION

paragraphs.text:
Independent organizations have provided guidance and frameworks
for integrating AI into educational practices in Türkiye. In 2023, the Artificial
Intelligence Policies Association (AIPA) published the document “Artificial
Intelligence in Education – Policies” 14 This guide prioritizes key areas, beginning
with the need for digital literacy, ensuring students and teachers have the skills to
utilize AI tools for education. AIPA’s framework emphasizes ethical AI awareness,
empowering students and teachers to recognize and address potential AI biases
and ethical issues. The document also outlines security measures, guidelines for
data security, fairness, and transparency, and raises awareness on concerns about
algorithmic bias and discrimination to ensure the inclusive design of AI systems.

title: 10 Artificial Intelligence in School Education in Türkiye

paragraphs.text:
Türkiye’s commitment to integrating AI into education is evident
not only in its policy frameworks but also in research and the organization
of conferences on the subject . Türkiye has contributed to the field of AI in
Education, producing research and development initiatives that reflect its
growing commitment to educational innovation. 15 Also, the Education Industry
and Technology Institute has organized several workshops focused on AI in
Education (AIEd). 16 Organizing seminars on AI in education is important for
equipping educators, policymakers, and stakeholders with the knowledge
required to better understand these emerging technologies. These workshops
could help to foster interdisciplinary collaboration, encourage responsible use
of AI in education, and contribute to the development of informed policies and
curricula.

Beyond organizing seminars, Türkiye’s Ministry of National
Education has taken steps to develop AI-based educational tools aimed at
enhancing learning . In collaboration with Istanbul Technical University (ITU), the
Ministry has worked on creating customized instructional materials that support
students’ learning. ITU has also contributed by conducting training sessions to
help educators understand and use AI technologies. Additionally, the Ministry’s
General Directorate of Innovation and Educational Technologies has announced
plans to introduce AI-related content across various educational levels, starting
from elementary school. As part of this initiative, the “Artificial Intelligence
Education for Children” project was launched, and under the guidance of
Manisa Celal Bayar University , research has been initiated to provide AI training
to students. 17 While these efforts reflect a commitment to integrating AI into
the Türkiye’s education system, the success of such initiatives depends not only
on technological development but also on ensuring equitable access, teacher
training and readiness, and the ethical use of AI in classroom settings.

A main driver behind Türkiye’s private sector vibrancy is the strategic
ecosystem fostered by the Education Technology Incubation and
Innovation Center (ETKİM) . The center was established by the MoNE at the
METU Teknokent campus (See Box 1).18 ETKİM serves as a pillar of the Türkiye’s
digital transformation by changing the focus from infrastructure investments
toward high-impact educational outputs. By bringing together entrepreneurs,
researchers, and educators, ETKİM serves as a catalyst for a vibrant EdTech sector,
ensuring that private innovation is closely aligned with national pedagogical
goals.

title: 3. AI powered educational tools and platforms

paragraphs.text:
In Türkiye’s school education, AI technologies are reshaping
teaching practices, learning experiences, and school management. For
students, locally developed platforms such as Madlen and MentalUP help
personalize learning, provide instant feedback, and increase motivation
through interactive exercises. Teachers can also use AI tools, including
Eğitimi Planla and Öğretmen Plus for lesson planning and creating
differentiated instructional materials. Moreover, school administrators have
begun integrating AI for optimizing communication, decision-making, and
operational efficiency. National initiatives led by the Ministry of National
Education (MoNE) such as the AI Education Guide for Teachers demonstrate
a structured effort to build AI literacy and responsible use among educators
and students. This chapter highlights the applications of AI tools across
students, teachers, and administrators in the context of primary and secondary
education.

Although AI tools offer potential for personalization and
scalability, their implementation must be balanced against ethical
dimensions . AI technologies that use student data raise concerns regarding
academic integrity, algorithmic bias, and the privacy of underage learners.
The implementation of these technologies requires strict adherence to data
protection standards, transparency, and the preservation of student rights (See
Box 2). Furthermore, automated scoring models may inadvertently perpetuate
existing biases related to linguistic background, gender, or socioeconomic
status (See Box 3). Recognizing these challenges, the Directorate General for
Innovation and Educational Technologies (DGIET) at the Ministry of National
Education has published the Recommendations on AI Ethics’ booklet. 19
This document stipulates an ethical framework for students, teachers, and
policymakers, offering guided principles to mitigate risks while maximizing
educational benefits. By establishing these guidelines, Türkiye’s government
reinforces its commitment to a responsible and human-centered AI adoption,
ensuring that technological progress is aligned with fundamental educational
values.

paragraphs.text: Box 2: Ethical and equity considerations

AI deployment that promotes equity and adheres to international standards integrates
the following pillars into their strategy:

1. Data governance : alignment with Türkiye’s Law on the Protection of Personal
Data (KVKK), ensuring regulatory frameworks oversight for student-centered AI.
2. Data privacy: protect students data and privacy, ensuring data processing for
underage is secure.
3. Inclusive design : usage of diverse datasets allows AI to recognize the different
socioeconomic realities and linguistic profiles across Türkiye’s provinces.
4. Audits: predictive models and assessment tools are tested to ensure results are
fair and consistent across all student contexts.
5. Equitable access: development is focused on AI tools with functionality for
low-connectivity environments, guaranteeing continuity regardless of location.
Source: Adapted from UNICEF (2025). Guidance on AI and children

title: 3.1 AI FOR STUDENTS

paragraphs.text:
This section explores how AI supports individualized learning in
three key areas: intelligent tutoring systems, classroom assignments,
and assessments. Through adaptive learning technologies, AI-driven
tutoring, and generative AI, teachers can now provide customized learning
paths that reflect students’ preferences, pacing, and skill levels. Intelligent
tutoring systems offer immediate feedback and support, while generative
AI helps create dynamic and interactive assignments. By exploring practical
examples and research, this section highlights how AI could boost student
engagement, enhance academic performance, and equip students with skills
for the modern world.

Educators and institutions in Türkiye increasingly prioritize
platforms that can adapt to diverse learning styles, preferences, and
academic needs . Building on AI’s potential to personalize learning, research
conducted in Türkiye emphasizes the importance of personalization as a
critical factor in selecting effective Learning Management Systems (LMS) for
educational settings. 20 In this context, AI emerges as a powerful enabler of
personalized learning experiences. By leveraging data-driven insights and
adaptive algorithms, AI can tailor content delivery, recommend resources,
and adjust learning trajectories in real time. This level of customization not
only enhances student engagement but also fosters a more inclusive and
supportive learning environment.

title: 3.1.1 PERSONALIZED LEARNING WITHIN CLASSROOMS

paragraphs.text:
Adaptive learning platforms and Intelligent tutoring systems (ITS)
are incorporating AI to create highly personalized learning experiences
for students . 21 AI powered ITS analyze student data such as engagement
levels, learning metrics, and student preferences, to dynamically tailor content,
pacing, and support to each student’s needs. Although more research is
needed on its effective design and scalability, leveraging AI to improve digital
personalized learning, shows great promise for improving student outcomes
and helping those who have fallen behind catch up. 22

Tutoring, whether from peers, parents, or professionals, is
an effective method for improving student learning across subjects
and grades . In fact, a large meta-analysis has shown that tutoring has a
significant positive impact, improving learning outcomes by an average of
0.37 standard deviations. 23 However, human-led tutoring faces significant
cost and scalability challenges. AI-powered tutoring could make the proven
benefits of personalized support available to more students cost-effectively.
For this to succeed, AI systems must be developed with “teachers in the loop,”
empowering educators to guide the implementation of AI tools, ensuring AI
serves as a supportive tool that enhances teacher instruction and improves
student learning.

Leveraging natural language processing (NLP), AI-powered
tutoring can engage students in human-like dialogues and provide
personalized instructional paths with immediate feedback . Notably,
studies have demonstrated that AI tutors offering intelligent support for
mathematics remediation can yield learning improvements comparable
to those achieved through one-on-one human instruction. 24 A U.S. survey
conducted to over 6,000 students and parents revealed a significant shift
from human tutors to ChatGPT. The findings showed that 85% of high school
students believe studying with ChatGPT is more effective than using a tutor. 25
Türkiye can take advantage and leverage AI-powered tutoring to supplement
classroom instruction, providing students with tools for remediation and
learning improvement.

Türkiye is significantly advancing its digital education systems by
integrating an AI-powered tutoring system, the EBA Student Assistant ,
directly into its primary educational portal, EBA . This tool provides students
with 24/7 access to personalized support. The system is designed to guide
students toward relevant educational content within the vast EBA library
and adapts to each student’s learning pace and needs, ensuring a tailored

title: 3.1.2 AI FOR ASSIGNMENTS

paragraphs.text:
The growing use of AI tools for schoolwork is raising concerns
about academic integrity . An increasing number of students are now turning
to ChatGPT and other AI applications to complete assignments, ranging from
writing essays to solving difficult problems. In fact, a study from the Center
for Democracy & Technology indicates that 59% of U.S. teachers believe their
students are using these tools for schoolwork. This perception is mirrored by
an increase in the adoption of AI-detection software, as 68% of educators
report using such technology to verify the originality of student submissions 30.

Over-relying on AI detection tools for education presents
substantial problems . As these tools are now imperfect can produce
false positives, leading to students being wrongly accused of academic
dishonesty. The dependency on AI detection tools can foster a climate of
mistrust that undermines the relationship between teachers and students,
which is essential for a healthy learning process. Therefore, it’s imperative for
educators in Türkiye to find a balance between maintaining academic integrity
and creating a supportive environment that encourages learning.

Instead of imposing outright bans on generative AI tools for
assignments, a more strategic and nuanced approach is necessary . Türkiye’s
educators should focus on developing assignments that demand higher-
order thinking, critical analysis, and personal insights—skills that current AI
technologies cannot replicate. For example, within Türkiye’s context, a history
teacher might move beyond essays that ask for a summary of the Ottoman
Empire’s rise. Instead, they could require students to analyze and compare
specific Ottoman and early Republican-era documents, arguing how societal
values shifted, a task that requires deep contextual understanding. Similarly,
Educators can implement more in-class writing exercises to gauge student
comprehension directly, or integrate multimedia and personal reflection
elements, which are difficult for AI to generate convincingly. 31 (See table 3 for
resources to deal with AI for assignments).

text:
The growing use of AI tools for schoolwork is raising concerns
about academic integrity . An increasing number of students are now turning
to ChatGPT and other AI applications to complete assignments, ranging from
writing essays to solving difficult problems. In fact, a study from the Center
for Democracy & Technology indicates that 59% of U.S. teachers believe their
students are using these tools for schoolwork. This perception is mirrored by
an increase in the adoption of AI-detection software, as 68% of educators
report using such technology to verify the originality of student submissions 30.
Over-relying on AI detection tools for education presents
substantial problems . As these tools are now imperfect can produce
false positives, leading to students being wrongly accused of academic
dishonesty. The dependency on AI detection tools can foster a climate of
mistrust that undermines the relationship between teachers and students,
which is essential for a healthy learning process. Therefore, it’s imperative for
educators in Türkiye to find a balance between maintaining academic integrity
and creating a supportive environment that encourages learning.
Instead of imposing outright bans on generative AI tools for
assignments, a more strategic and nuanced approach is necessary . Türkiye’s
educators should focus on developing assignments that demand higher-
order thinking, critical analysis, and personal insights—skills that current AI
technologies cannot replicate. For example, within Türkiye’s context, a history
teacher might move beyond essays that ask for a summary of the Ottoman
Empire’s rise. Instead, they could require students to analyze and compare
specific Ottoman and early Republican-era documents, arguing how societal
values shifted, a task that requires deep contextual understanding. Similarly,
Educators can implement more in-class writing exercises to gauge student
comprehension directly, or integrate multimedia and personal reflection
elements, which are difficult for AI to generate convincingly. 31 (See table 3 for
resources to deal with AI for assignments).

Educational institutions should prioritize teaching students how
to use AI tools responsibly for their schoolwork, emphasizing academic
integrity . By providing students with the necessary digital literacy skills to
navigate this new technological landscape, educators can foster a generation
of informed and responsible technology users, in line with national technology
goals. A useful parallel can be drawn with existing educational practices. For
instance, just as a calculator might be permitted for a complex engineering
problem or a project assignment but prohibited during a university entrance
practice exam that tests fundamental mathematical knowledge, the use of
tools like ChatGPT could be strategically allowed. AI might be permitted
for assignments focused on higher-order skills like creative brainstorming
or data analysis. However, for assessments designed to evaluate a student’s
foundational knowledge, such as a traditional written exam its use would
need to be restricted.

title: 3.1.3 AI FOR STUDENT ASSESSMENT

paragraphs.text:
Integrating AI technologies into Türkiye’s educational assessment
processes holds the potential to increase efficiency, reduce bias, and
offer personalized evaluations . When teachers use formative assessments
sporadically, the lack of frequent data on student learning outcomes prevents
schools from having the agility required to adapt promptly to evolving student
learning needs. By incorporating AI into assessments, educators can gain
continuous, data-driven insights into learning trends, allowing for the timely
identification of a student’s strengths and areas needing improvement long
before high-stakes exams such as Türkiye’s LGS High School Entrance Exam . 32
Furthermore, AI can improve the capacity to evaluate time-consuming,
non-standardized work like project assignments or open-ended questions,
providing valuable data to inform classroom instruction. 33

The advancements in AI have also brought potential risks to the
assessment and evaluation landscape . Issues concerning the validity,
reliability, transparency, fairness, and equity of assessments highlight the
need for careful planning when implementing AI technologies for student
assessments. 34 A major concern is algorithmic bias that could reinforce
existing regional or socioeconomic disparities in educational outcomes (See
Box 3). Furthermore, ensuring the privacy and security of student data is a
critical issue that must be handled in compliance with Türkiye’s Personal Data
Protection Law (KVKK) . 35 These risks emphasize the critical need for AI systems
for assessments to be evaluated, debiased, and monitored before being
deployed. This is especially true for high-stakes, centralized assessments like
the LGS, which determines the educational future of millions of students.
Implementing these technologies without such safeguards could undermine
public trust and the principle of equal opportunity in Türkiye’s education
system.

paragraphs.text: Box 3: Algorithmic Bias

Algorithmic bias occurs when an AI system works systematically better or worse for
different groups of people. It is a “skewed” way of making decisions that creates unfair
advantages for some and disadvantages for others based on traits like race, gender, or
class. The negative effects of bias can be grouped in two categories:

1. Unfair distribution : Occurs when an AI unfairly “hands out” or “withholds” an op-
portunity or resource. For example, in education, an AI grading system could
give lower scores to students from specific backgrounds, or a “predictor” tool
could unfairly block certain students from high-stakes admissions.
2. Unfair portrayal : Occurs when an AI reinforces stereotypes or makes certain
groups “invisible.” For example:
a. Stereotyping: An image search that only shows one gender for certain

high-paying professions.
b. Denigration: A search engine associating specific names with negative

terms.
c. Under-representation: When a group is missing or poorly represented in
the data, making the AI fail to recognize them accurately.

Source: Baker, R.S., Hawn, A. Algorithmic Bias in Education. Int J Artif Intell Educ 32, 1052–1092 (2022).
https://doi.org/10.1007/s40593-021-00285-9

Various automated grading platforms are available, each offering
unique benefits applicable to Türkiye’s education system . For instance,
some platforms such as GradeScope are designed to significantly reduce the
time teachers spend grading exams and assignments, ensure more consistent
and fair scoring, and enhance the quality of feedback. A key advantage is
the ability to help educators quickly identify common student mistakes
across a classroom, providing valuable insights for future lessons. This tool
is particularly useful for STEM courses like mathematics and physics, as they
allow for the digital grading of traditional paper-based work. Furthermore,
a growing number of AI tools such as Essay Grader are now available for
the automated grading of essays, which could be a major asset for teachers
in subjects like Turkish Language and Literature. See table 4 for a list of AI

title: 3.1.4 SYNTHESIS – AI FOR STUDENTS

paragraphs.text:
In sum, the evidence regarding AI integration in Türkiye’s educational
sector, particularly through platforms for students like the EBA Student Assistant
reveals a shift toward data-driven personalization. The analysis indicates that
intelligent tutoring systems (ITS) and adaptive learning platforms can offer learning
gains comparable to human instruction while addressing scalability challenges.
However, the data also suggests that without specific safeguards, generative AI
tools can lead to “passive learning” and potential declines in problem-solving
skills, as seen in recent large-scale student studies. Moreover, quality assurance
protocols would be required to monitor algorithmic bias to avoid a risk to the
fairness of high-stakes assessments like the LGS exam.

The transition toward AI-enhanced education would benefit from a
more strategic, “human-in-the-loop” approach to ensure both quality and
equity. 36 Rather than an outright adoption of automated tools, the analysis
points toward the necessity of establishing clear oversight mechanisms
where educators validate AI outputs and ground technology in proven
pedagogical principles. It appears advisable for institutions to prioritize the
development of assignments that emphasize higher-order thinking, which AI
cannot easily replicate, while simultaneously updating national frameworks to
include transparent auditing of algorithms. By moving from a purely technical
implementation to a collaborative model between AI and human expertise,
Türkiye has the opportunity to harness these tools to foster a more inclusive
and resilient educational environment .

Artificial intelligence is already providing tangible advantages for
teachers , most notably by saving time through the automation of resource
creation, simplification of lesson planning, and streamlining of administrative
tasks. A survey of over 2,600 education faculty and students in the United
States revealed the diverse ways teachers are integrating AI such as running
prompts to anticipate student outputs, instructing students on its proper use,
and designing more dynamic classroom activities (see Graph 1). 37 As more
teachers recognize the time-saving potential and assistive capabilities of AI to
relieve faculty of manual processes,38 their usage is rapidly gaining traction
within the teaching profession.39

In the context of Türkiye’s educational landscape, while the sentiment
towards AI in education is becoming more positive, disparities in confidence
and perceived usability exist within the teaching community . Findings
from an online survey of 448 math and science teachers in Türkiye indicate a
broadly positive disposition towards AI. However, the results also highlighted
a significant gender difference, with male educators demonstrating higher self-
efficacy and perceiving AI as easier to use than their female counterparts. This
suggests that while these STEM teachers are generally open to adopting AI,
targeted interventions are needed to address this gender disparity and improve
the technology’s overall ease of use. 40

As Türkiye seeks to modernize its education system, strengthening teachers’
digital competences becomes an essential foundation for the effective and ethical
adoption of AI-based educational innovations.

Focusing on Türkiye’s educational system, this section examines key
areas where AI is impacting educators : the development of lesson plans and
instructional content, support for professional development, and the reduction of
administrative workloads. It demonstrates how AI tools can empower teachers in
Türkiye to enhance their effectiveness and better respond to the diverse needs of
their students.
Box 4: Digital Ecosystem for Teacher Training Project

The Digital Ecosystem for Teacher Training Project was launched to enhance the quality
of the digital education and training ecosystem and to ensure that teachers provide better
services to all children by developing their capacities to meet the requirements of the labor
market. The Project has delivered five foundational pillars to enhance educators’ digital
capabilities:

1. Digital Teacher Competences Framework (DETT) : This framework identifies 14 com-
petences, 17 sub-competences, and 380 indicators. It categorizes skills into begin-
ner, intermediate, and advanced levels across three dimensions: awareness, func-
tionality, and actuality.
2. Teacher Learning Monitoring and Evaluation System (TLMES) & ÖBA Integration : The
project upgraded the ÖBA interface with a new question bank, improved moder-
ation screens, and Learning Record System (LRS) integration. The accompanying
TLMES records real-time teacher interactions and learning metrics, providing evi-
dence-based data to refine future professional development strategies.
3. Digital Competency Training Pack (DCTP) : A 10-module, 120-hour interactive on-
line program for teacher digital skills and competences development that is aligned
with the DETT. This training pack features emulators for hands-on practice, interac-
tive storylines, and performance tasks to ensure applied learning and genuine skill
development.
4. Teacher Learning Labs : Eight active labs established in seven pilot provinces to pro-
vide collaborative spaces equipped with professional audio and visual recording
areas, enabling teachers to create high-quality e-content for educational purposes.
5. Network of Facilitators : A cohort of 399 trained teachers supports the ecosystem
by evaluating participant performance tasks through standardized rubrics and pro-
viding feedback. Facilitators offer technical guidance, contribute to the assessment
question bank, and conduct face-to-face meetings with teachers in their schools to
disseminate the project results. Facilitators have visited nearly 4,000 schools and
shared information with 110,000 teachers about the project’s benefits.
Source: Digital Ecosystem for Teacher Training Project

1. Digital Teacher Competences Framework (DETT) : This framework identifies 14 com-
petences, 17 sub-competences, and 380 indicators. It categorizes skills into begin-
ner, intermediate, and advanced levels across three dimensions: awareness, func-
tionality, and actuality.
2. Teacher Learning Monitoring and Evaluation System (TLMES) & ÖBA Integration : The
project upgraded the ÖBA interface with a new question bank, improved moder-
ation screens, and Learning Record System (LRS) integration. The accompanying
TLMES records real-time teacher interactions and learning metrics, providing evi-
dence-based data to refine future professional development strategies.
3. Digital Competency Training Pack (DCTP) : A 10-module, 120-hour interactive on-
line program for teacher digital skills and competences development that is aligned
with the DETT. This training pack features emulators for hands-on practice, interac-
tive storylines, and performance tasks to ensure applied learning and genuine skill
development.
4. Teacher Learning Labs : Eight active labs established in seven pilot provinces to pro-
vide collaborative spaces equipped with professional audio and visual recording
areas, enabling teachers to create high-quality e-content for educational purposes.
5. Network of Facilitators : A cohort of 399 trained teachers supports the ecosystem
by evaluating participant performance tasks through standardized rubrics and pro-
viding feedback. Facilitators offer technical guidance, contribute to the assessment
question bank, and conduct face-to-face meetings with teachers in their schools to
disseminate the project results. Facilitators have visited nearly 4,000 schools and
shared information with 110,000 teachers about the project’s benefits.
Source: Digital Ecosystem for Teacher Training Project

environment, accelerating their ability to participate in classrooms.
2. Personalizing education for displaced students: Refugee children often face
“broken” education paths due to displacement. AI serves as a tool for academic
remediation.
a. Diagnostic assessments: AI-driven platforms can identify specific learn-

ing gaps and create a remediation path focused on missing foundational
skills.
b. Pacing: For students dealing with the trauma of displacement, AI can of-

fer a self-paced environment, reducing the “performance anxiety” often
found in high-pressure settings
3. Key challenges:
a. Accessibility: The benefits of AI are only realized if the digital divide is

bridged. Refugee families often lack high-speed connectivity or devices
required to run AI tutoring systems.
b. Data vulnerability: Storing information of refugees requires enhanced

KVKK protocols to ensure data is never used for non-educational surveil-
lance.
c. Cultural bias: AI models struggle with diverse accents or cultural idioms.

If the AI is not trained on representative data from these communities, it
may provide inaccurate feedback.

AI tools have the potential to evolve Türkiye’s central educational
platform - EBA . An AI-powered EBA could allow subject-teacher groups
to share lesson plans developed with the support of Türkiye’s AI Teacher
Assistant and to co-edit them in real-time, integrating the most effective
practices from different schools. Advanced features, such as an intelligent
search that pinpoints the perfect resource within the EBA library or a system
that recommends successful teaching strategies based on a teacher’s specific
needs, would make professional collaboration more efficient and impactful,
directly supporting the goals of Türkiye’s schools and the MoNE.

While AI lesson planning tools offer a way to combine structured
pedagogy with teacher flexibility in Türkiye, their implementation
demands careful oversight . For these tools to succeed, the Ministry of
National Education (MoNE) has to ensure their algorithms are vetted for
accuracy and inclusivity. The principle must be clear: AI serves as a helpful
assistant, but the teacher’s professional expertise and judgment remain
central to the classroom. When designed this way, AI tools can reduce
teachers’ planning time and enhance the quality of instruction nationwide.

title: 3.2.2 AI FOR TEACHER PROFESSIONAL DEVELOPMENT

AI-powered tools for professional development can improve
teacher support by providing personalized guidance at every stage of
a teacher’s career . For those in pre-service training, AI can serve as a study
partner, answering questions on topics like teaching methods and classroom
management. For current teachers, AI offers real-time feedback and practical
support during in-service training. Additionally, AI can polish teaching
practices by observing and analyzing lessons. These customized approaches
have the potential to improve teacher effectiveness and retention, ultimately
harnessing AI’s potential to elevate the quality of education systems (See
table 6 for a list of key elements required in AI for professional development).

While in-service training programs such as ÖBA are vital for
upskilling teachers, it is also important to focus on the next generation of
educators through pre-service training . The future success of AI in schools
depends on the collaboration between the Ministry of National Education,
Türkiye’s Council of Higher Education , and university education faculties
to include AI literacy and pedagogy into their curriculum. Using AI tools as
“digital mentors” during pre-service training can provide teacher candidates
with continuous support, ensuring they are prepared to lead modern, AI-
driven classrooms upon graduation. 50 This dual focus on both in-service and
pre-service training is essential for a comprehensive national strategy.

In addition to pre-service training, AI is creating pathways for
teacher professional development through classroom observation and
feedback tools . These technologies offer a data-driven complement to
the traditional school inspection systems, shifting the focus from periodic
evaluation to continuous coaching. For instance, tools like TeachFX use voice
AI to analyze classroom discourse, providing teachers with objective data
on student engagement. A recent randomized controlled trial in the United
States demonstrated that teachers who received automated feedback on
their questioning techniques significantly improved this practice by 20%
compared to a control group after just five weeks. 51 Interviews confirmed
that teachers found the feedback valuable for reflection and growth. By
integrating such a tool into the Teacher Information Network, Türkiye could
offer every teacher a personalized AI instructional coach; however, for
successful implementation in the country, all data processing would need to
comply strictly with the Personal Data Protection Law – KVKK . When combined
with tailored professional development, such AI tools have the potential to
provide the personalized, scalable support needed to enhance teaching
quality.

While the integration of AI into Türkiye’s schools offers powerful
tools, it also presents challenges for teachers . While the promise of AI to
improve education in Türkiye is noteworthy, a recent study highlights a gap
between potential and practice. Research involving 66 teachers across different
disciplines found that although AI tools like MagicSchool and ChatGPT were
valued for their adaptability, the implementation has had challenges such
as technical issues, curriculum misalignment, ethical concerns, and cultural
barriers. The study suggests that without a plan to overcome specific cultural,
ethical, and structural barriers, the power of AI in Türkiye’s education system
will remain untapped. 52 While AI promises to streamline administrative tasks
and enhance the teaching and learning process, but also demands that
educators adapt to new methodologies beyond their traditional training. This

title: 3.2.3 SYNTHESIS – AI FOR TEACHERS

paragraphs.text:
The integration of AI within Türkiye’s teaching profession is
characterized by openness offset by disparities in digital self-efficacy and
technical proficiency. While the development of local AI tools and platforms
like Eğitimi Planla demonstrates an institutional commitment to supporting
teachers, the “readiness” of the teaching workforce remains non-uniform.
Current research indicates that while STEM educators in Türkiye hold a broadly
positive disposition toward AI, only a small fraction of the teaching population
(approximately 3%) currently achieves “Pioneer” status in digital competence.

The successful adoption of AI tools among Türkiye’s teachers
depends on moving beyond tool access toward a comprehensive strategy
of pedagogical empowerment. Rather than viewing AI as a replacement for
teacher tasks, it appears beneficial to frame these technologies as “digital
assistants” that support the instructional process. To address the identified
gaps in competency, it is advisable for national strategies to prioritize dual-
track training—focusing on both in-service upskilling via platforms like ÖBA
and the integration of AI literacy into pre-service university curricula.
